newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia assistant treasurer quits over bank stake.
newsitem.headline: Australia assistant treasurer quits over bank stake.

text.p: Assistant Treasurer Jim Short, the junior minister responsible for banking policy, resigned Sunday following controversy over his ownership of shares in a major bank, Prime Minister John Howard announced.
"The assistant treasurer, Senator Jim Short, has tendered his resignation from the ministry," Howard said in a statement. "I have accepted that resignation."
Howard said Short's position in the ministry would be taken by Rod Kemp, a senator from Victoria and brother of David Kemp, junior minister for schools, vocational education and training.

Under the ministerial guidelines drawn up by Howard's government, ministers are required to divest themselves of all shares and similar interests in any company or business involved in the area of their portfolio responsibilities.
Howard said last week that he had considered firing Short for failing to reveal that his family company held shares in Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, known as ANZ.
Howard said then that he decided not to sack Short for breaching ministerial guidelines because he considered the shareholding to be an oversight.
However, more information came to light over the weekend, when Short told Howard that his office had discovered that in June he had given routine approval for a bank license for an ANZ subsidiary.
"Now that my attention has been drawn to that approval, I feel that the circumstances of the matter have changed," Short said in a resignation letter released by Howard.
Short, 59, said last week he had taken steps to dispose of his 6,679 shares, worth about A$48,000 (US$38,000) based on Friday's closing price on the stock exchange.
